spec: ALGORITHMS 1.1 (lines) and 1.3 (what a text file is)
about: Given the bytes of a git blob, the lines of the file, or null if the blob is not text. `bytes` is a list of parts that are concatenated: {"utf8": "..."} is that text encoded as UTF-8, {"hex": ".."} is raw bytes, {"fill": "61", "count": N} is that one byte N times. Exactly one of `lines` (an array, or null for not text) or `lineCount` (when the lines are too long to write out) is given.

cases.name: a trailing newline does not start another line
no trailing newline keeps the last line
empty content has no lines
a lone newline is one empty line
two newlines are two empty lines
one CR before each LF is dropped
CRLF with no final newline
mixed LF and CRLF lines
a UTF-8 byte order mark is not part of line 1
a byte order mark alone leaves no lines
U+2028 is an ordinary character, not a line break
U+0085 is an ordinary character, not a line break
a form feed is an ordinary character, not a line break
non-ASCII text is kept
a stray 0xff byte is not well-formed UTF-8, so the file is not text
an overlong encoding of "/" is not text
an encoded surrogate is not text
a code point above U+10FFFF is not text
a truncated multi-byte sequence is not text
a CR that is not followed by LF is not text
two CRs before an LF are not text
a CR at the very end is not text
a NUL byte in the first 8000 bytes is binary
a NUL byte in the very first byte is binary
a NUL after the first 8000 bytes is not looked for: the content is one (odd) line
